# Phase 6: Research portfolio, technical discussion, job talk, behavioral

*weeks 23–24, then continuous* · [Track on the site](https://arubad.github.io/AI_Research_Journey/#p6)

Research gets you the interview; this phase makes sure you can defend it. Alisa's framing: the technical-discussion round is the most underrated, and the behavioral round is the one she failed first by assuming she was "obviously well-behaved" and then going blank.

**Build the portfolio (AGENT-heavy, HAND-defensible).** As a student without a PhD paper trail, your CV projects are the research record. Aim for three public projects by week 20, each with a hypothesis, an ablation, a plot, and a README written in the "why I did it" voice:

1. One from the Phase 3 break-it experiments (see the CV note at the end of Phase 3).
2. One systems project: a from-scratch GPT-2 124M reproduction on [build-nanogpt](https://github.com/karpathy/build-nanogpt) with your own throughput log, or [CS336 A2](https://github.com/stanford-cs336/assignment2-systems)'s FlashAttention-2 Triton kernel with a benchmark table.
3. One post-training project: the mini-GRPO or DPO run from [CS336 A5](https://github.com/stanford-cs336/assignment5-alignment), with reward curves and a failure-mode study (β = 0, G = 2).

For each, the HAND core (model, loss, loop) is yours; the harness, sweeps and plots are the agent's; and you must be able to answer "why is this line here?" for every file. Write the design-choice list before you consider a project done.

**Technical and research discussion prep.** For every project, write a one-page "why" narrative, not a "what" summary: every major design choice with its defensible reason, what you tried that failed, what you would do differently, and what you would do with 10x the compute. Form opinions on three to five research directions you believe in right now. Tailor the pitch to the role: interviewers are tired, so hit the keywords of the team's area.

**Rapid-fire set, out loud.** Drill the rapid-fire set out loud, with AI as the examiner: ways to encode position; 5D parallelism; PPO vs GRPO; pre- vs post-norm; LoRA layer choice; why Flash Attention is faster without changing the math; the KV-cache formula; Chinchilla's N* and D*. Read the target company's last six months of papers and reference them naturally.

**Job talk (if asked).** 45–60 minutes, 80%+ on first-author or lead-author work, second-author and ongoing work in the last 10 minutes. Expect deep Q&A on every baseline and experimental choice; rehearse with people who push back hard.

**Behavioral.** Write down five to ten memorable stories now and map each to leadership, conflict, failure, impact, collaboration in STAR form, so retrieval is instant. Prepare specific answers to "Why this company?" and to "What is your view on AI safety and responsible development?" — frontier labs ask the second one seriously and want a considered position. After every interview, record notes the same day; they feed the next cram.

## In this folder
| Path | What goes there |
| --- | --- |
| `projects.md` | The three public repos, each with its hypothesis, ablation and plot |
| `narratives/` | One-page "why" narrative per project |
| `rapid-fire.md` | Your spoken-answer notes for the rapid-fire set |
| `job-talk/` | Slides and rehearsal notes |

Behavioral stories are personal; keep them in a private repo or notes app, not here.
